# The Planet That Wanders and the God Who Doesn't

## Scripture

*"You, Lord, laid the foundation of the earth in times past, and the heavens are the work of your hands. They will perish, but you remain; they will all wear out like a garment. Like clothing you will change them and they will be discarded. But you remain the same, and your years will never end."* — Psalm 102:25–27

## Reflection

Watch the sky long enough this fall, and you'll notice something unsettling: the planets wander. Mars drifts against the backdrop of fixed stars, Jupiter traces a slow and looping path, Venus appears, vanishes, returns. Ancient astronomers called them *planetes*—wanderers—because they refused to stay put.

We wander too. Seasons shift, plans unravel, certainties loosen their grip. Sometimes we look at our own lives and see only a meandering path.

But here is the quiet gift hidden in the wandering: the planets are not lost. Their motion is governed by laws so precise that eclipses can be predicted centuries in advance. What looks like drift from earth is, from above, perfect orbit. The wanderers are held.

And the One who holds them does not wander. Psalm 102 sets the heavens and their Maker side by side: the skies will wear out like old clothing, but God remains. Same yesterday, today, and forever. The God who keeps the planets in their patient circles keeps you as well. Your orbit may feel unpredictable—but you are not unheld.

## Prayer

Lord of the wandering lights and the fixed stars, thank you that when everything in my life feels like it's drifting, you remain the same. Hold me in the orbit of your faithful love, and teach me to trust the One who keeps the planets in their course. In Jesus' name, amen.
